title: KL boundary search for bitwidth and quant safety gates
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Build an automated boundary-search system that finds the bitwidth/quant-profile breakpoints where model output fidelity (measured via KL divergence + embedding cosine + human sample checks) crosses a tolerated threshold. The goal is to produce per-model, per-cohort safety gates used by runtime routing and rollout policies so we can automatically choose quant profiles (AWQ/GPTQ, int8/int4) without surprising quality regressions.

Scope:
- Implement a KL-based binary/bisect search across quant profiles and bitwidths to identify smallest-safe profile under SLOs.
- Support both AWQ and GPTQ pipelines, capturing layer-wise contribution signals.
- Tie the search to cohort split evaluation (by prompt type / seq length / usage bucket) and compute cohort-specific thresholds.
- Produce a gate artifact: quant_profile_safe = {cohort_id: [profiles passing checks], thresholds: {kl, embed_cosine, lm-perp_delta}}.
- Hook results into Console and rollout config: runtime can decline a candidate profile or route to higher-fidelity variant when budget or latency constraints require it.

Why this is different: Existing work focuses on fixed thresholding or post-hoc regression alerts. This ticket builds an active search that (a) finds the boundary, (b) characterizes which layers cause regressions (AWQ/GPTQ differences), and (c) produces deterministic gates that are used by the serving layer during A/B and canary rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Automated search job that runs on a model snapshot and returns the minimal quant profile passing criteria for a provided cohort (script + runner)
Cohort-level report with KL, embedding cosine, and summary human-sample flags for each candidate profile
Dashboard panel showing boundary curve (profile vs KL) and layer-sensitivity heatmap for AWQ and GPTQ
Gate artifact format documented and accepted by runtime (JSON spec and example); runtime integration PR opened
Can run end-to-end on 2 production models (one LLM-7B class, one LLM-30B class) and produce stable gates with reproducible thresholds
steps: Design experiment spec and gating criteria (this doc + Confluence link)
Add KL + embedding cos scorer to eval-harness and expose per-layer deltas for AWQ/GPTQ
Implement binary/bisect search runner that tries decreasing bitwidth/quant aggressiveness until tolerance breach
Run search across cohorts, generate gate artifacts and layer sensitivity maps
Create dashboard panels and integration PR to runtime for gate consumption
Schedule human spot-check pass on flagged boundary samples and incorporate feedback into threshold tuning
metrics: Primary: mean per-token KL divergence vs FP32 baseline (cohorted)
Secondary: embedding cosine similarity (avg), LM perplexity delta, token-level token-flip rate
Operational: time-to-compute-boundary (minutes per model), number of profiles tested per run
Business: estimated tokens saved if runtime uses minimal-safe profile vs conservative baseline
